3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Zaminder of Sree Faltani and to the waqf estate of Baliyadi Zaminder; that the then British government acquired the suit land measuring 125 acres including other land of this area for certain period for converting this area as government forest land by notification No. 1139 dated 14-11-1951 after serving notice upon the Zaminder and local people on 11-8-1951; that SA and RS khatian were correctly prepared in the names of the government and the forest department; that again, the suit land was permanently acquired by the government vide notification No. 4836 LR and No. 4849 LR dated 2-4-1956 and thus the suit land was permanently vested in the government and forest department annulling all the rights of the Zaminder therein and that the suit land has already been in the control and possession of the government as per notification No. XII / Forest 13-19 /85 /19 dated 31-3-1985 under section 4 of the Forest Act. It is further contended that the suit land has been entered into the Khatian of Forest Department; that the office of Divisional Forest Officer is located at Moakhali that there is no office of Forest Department at Kaliakore; that in order to suppress the summons, the address of the Divisional Forest Officer was shown at Kaliakore; that summons was not served upon the Divisional Forest Officer in Title Suit No. 329 of 1974; that suppressing the summons collusively and on practising fraud upon the Court, the defendants illegally obtained ex parte decree on 4-12-1975 and that the defendants in order to grab the forest land created some forged papers. It is further stated that the appearance of the Government pleader and filing of written statement was fraudulently shown; that the suit land was all along in the possession of Forest Department; that the defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land; that knowing about the ex prrte decree in title Suit No.329 of 1974 on 4-12-1975 from Misc. case No. 4 of 1968 of ADC (Rev), Gazipur, the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of the ex parte decree void and for declaration of title in respect of the suit land. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1 to 6, 7 and 8 filed written statements, inter alia, denying the material allegations contained in the plaint. 

 5. The case of the defendant Nos.1 to 6, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the khas possession of then Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkar Roy of Showapur, PS Dhamria whose interest was that of a tenure holder in respect of the suit property and his name was recorded as such in the CS khatian and in the relevant registers and that while having such tenure interest, the said Zaminder by an unregistered amalnama dated 15th Poush 1344 BS settled the suit land to Md Abdul Gafur, who took physical possession of the said land after obtaining such allotment and since then they have been possessing the land by annually selling the jungles to the buyers who took the same for cutting and taking away the shrubs and trees for use as fuel. It is further contended that Abdul Gafur died leaving 6 sons namely, Serajul Islam, Furat Ali, Abdul Balek, Noya Miah, Chanda Lai and Elihi Box; that the heirs of Abdul Gafur were also in possession of suit land; that Serajul Islam and the other heirs of Serajul Islam filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 against the Department of Forest for permanent injunction restraining them from disturbing their peaceful possession; that summons of that suit was properly served; that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement but lastly, he did not turn up and ultimately the suit was decreed ex parte on 4-12-1975. 

 8. It is further contended that heirs of Abdul Gafur executed a Power of Attorney in favour of Md Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, to sell and manage the suit land; that power of attorney holder Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa; sold 7.31 acres of land by a registered kabala dated 19-9-1989 in favour of this defendant who has been possessing the suit land after mutating his name; that the suit land was not acquired by the government; that no notice of acquisition was served upon the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 and other interested persons; that the acquisition is illegal and ineffective and that the plaintiff has no title and possession in the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be set aside. 

 9. The defendant No. 8 also filed a separate written statement, inter alia, contending that Abdul Gafur acquiring the suit land by way of amalnama died leaving defendant Nos. 1 to 6; that defendant Nos. 1 to 6 filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1974 for permanent injunction and obtained ex parte decree; that the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 having title and possession executed and registered a power of attorney on 15-12-1977 in favour of Md Ashan and his wife Ayatennessa who transferred 21.511/2 acres of land in favour of this defendant; that the boundary of his land was measured by an employee of ADC (Rev.), Gazipur; that getting possession he constructed but thereon and possessed other land through bargader. 

 16. Mr SM Enamul Hoque, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, has placed before us the plaint, w7itten statement, deposition and documents of the parties and the impugned judgment. 

 18. Mr Zahidul Bari, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 7, submits that the suit land originally belonged to Zaminder Babu Khamata Kinkor Roy who leased out the suit land to Abdul Gafur; that CS and SA record were prepared in the name of Abdul Gafur; that Abdul Gafur died. leaving 6 sons who executed and registered the power of attorney in favour of Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, to sell and manage the property and that by virtue of that power of attorney Ashan and his wife, Ayatennessa, sold 7.31 acres of land by registered kabala deed dated 19-9-1989 in favour of this defendant No. 7 who have been possessing the land and mutated his name. He further submits that the suit was not acquired by the government; that no notice of acquisition was served by the defendant Nos. 1 to 6 and other interested persons; that the acquisition is illegal and ineffective and that the government has no right, title and interest in the suit land. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur, was quite justified in passing the impugned judgment and thus he committed no illegality in passing the impugned judgment which does not call for any interference. He further submits that the suit is barred by limitation and the suit was not preferred by proper person, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 26. The defendants-respondents claim that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement in that suit. But the plaintiff-appellant categorically denies such assertion. The defendants respondents failed to file any scrap of paper or adduce any evidence to show that the learned Government pleader appeared and filed written statement in that case. This assertion of the defendants-respondents has fallen flat without any evidence. Before decreeing the suit ex parte, the Court must be satisfied as to the proof of service of summons upon the defendants and the claim of the plaintiff by cogent evidence. An ex parte decree may be set aside on either of the two grounds i.e. non-service of summons on the defendants or the defendants were prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit was taken up for hearing. 

 27. From the materials on record, it becomes manifestly clear that summons upon the defendants were not at all served or there is nothing on record to show that the government appeared and contested that suit. Thus it is evident that the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the suit No. 329 of 1974 was called on for hearing. Moreover, it is worthy to state that when the elements of fraud and collusion is manifested in procuring the ex parte decree, that decree vitiates. 

 28. The proposition of law emerging out of the authorities is that in ex parte disposal of the suit, the Court is required to observe minimum legal requirement and the order should show application of the Court's judicial mind as to whether the plaintiff's witnesses and other papers produced proved the plaintiff's case. The duty of a Court is to administer justice in accordance with law, Courts are required not to exercise punitive jurisdiction by depriving defendant. Our law of procedure is also designed to facilitate justice. The laws of procedure are grounded on the principle that a litigant public and a citizen should not be condemned unheard and decision should not be reached behind his back. The proceedings that affect his properties should be heard in his presence. The Court possesses a discretion to undo injustice caused to the citizens of the state and the Court must exercise that discretion. The hands of the Court are not tied by the ex parte orders. Mandate of law is that interference must be called for in a case like this. In this context, it is significant to point out that in furtherance of the ends of justice Court always leans in favour of setting aside an ex parte decree/order, rather than maintain the same because Court exists for the advancement of justice not to deprive a litigant of his right. 

 36. Moreover, the law relating to the retention of khas land in the possession of tenant is envisaged in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951. 

 37. Section 43 of the Act provides for publishing a notification declaring that compensation assessment roll in respect of any village or group of villages or local area has been finally published. Sub-section (3) of section 44 of the Act provides that all interests of raiyats etc. in non-retainable khas land other than the interest which has already been acquired under any other provision of the Act i.e. section 3 under Chapter II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government free from all encumbrances from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication in the official Gazette. On the other hand, sub-section 1 of the said section 44 provides that all interest of rent receivers in the estates, tenures and all other rent receiving interests in any holding or tenancy or in the non-retainable khas land other than the interest already acquired under Chapter-II or sub-section 3 of section 46E shall be deemed to have been acquired by the government and vest absolutely in the government from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification in the official gazette. Thus, reading of section 20, 43, and 44 of the Act together, we have no option but to hold that non-retainable khas land belonging either to the rent receiver or to the tenant shall be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vested in the government with the publication of a notification about final publication of the compensation assessment roll in the official gazette from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification. 

 38. Sub-section (1) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides that "on the acquisition of interest of rent receivers in any area under Chapter V, no rent receiver, cultivating raiyat, cultivating under-raiyat of non-agricultural tenant shall be entitled to retain possession of any of his khas lands in such area except as provided in sub-section,(2)."
